eligibilityRule: Every documented callable in the selected published root entrypoint is implemented for its typed input domain, all available upstream assertions plus added package-contract vectors pass, npm and LilScript app contracts match, and the LilScript port compiles to JavaScript, C, and a native executable.

ports.notes: This is the complete independently published @motionone/easing package. It is a Motion ecosystem component, not a claim that motion@13 is ported.
All documented numeric behavior is implemented. Invalid dynamic JavaScript values are rejected statically by LilScript rather than coerced at runtime.
The additional vectors verify BMP and surrogate-pair UTF-16 behavior.

The port preserves the package's prefix/suffix trimming, one-vector dynamic program, and UTF-16 code-unit behavior. Its function-local work array is verified as non-observable mutation by purity analysis.

The complete string-to-base36 API is implemented with typed signed bitwise operations, explicit unsigned radix serialization, and source-written Math.imul where upstream manually simulates its exact low-32-bit result.

The published package contains no upstream test files. Eighteen fixed package-contract assertions cover both algorithms and the documented default murmur3 alias before dense differential vectors. Source-written Math.imul replaces the upstream low/high-half simulation without enabling compiler-introduced imul.

auditedButIneligible.reason: The 312-export root and DOM animation engine are not implemented; it remains context-only in the application lab.
Exact compatibility requires symbol event keys, wildcard payload unions, and the public handler Map contract.
The complete package requires secure host randomness, custom random byte generators, CLI behavior, and string character extraction.
Its API is recursive variadic unknown input over arrays and dynamic object keys.
Its public API includes getters and Symbol.iterator semantics.
Its eight-function robust geometry root is audited as a high-value next port, but the 2,300-line adaptive expansion implementation is not yet rewritten or compatibility-gated.
